subject.title: macOS: Gateway daemon PATH excludes user bin dirs (nix, bun, local, etc.)

question: Should macOS managed Gateway services allow user/package-manager bin directories in PATH by default, expose a narrow opt-in, or keep the canonical system PATH only?
rationale: The source evidence is clear, but changing this behavior alters the daemon command-resolution trust boundary and conflicts with current docs/tests that encode a hardened macOS PATH policy.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in
options.body: Keep the canonical default and add a documented, doctor-aware service PATH opt-in for operators who accept the package-manager PATH trust tradeoff.

options.title: Change macOS default
options.body: Include Darwin user-bin directories by default, accepting the broader command-resolution surface for better Nix/Bun/local-bin discoverability.

options.title: Keep current policy
options.body: Reject daemon PATH expansion and document `tools.exec.pathPrepend` or explicit service-management alternatives for users who need extra command lookup paths.

recommendation.title: Add explicit opt-in
recommendation.body: Keep the canonical default and add a documented, doctor-aware service PATH opt-in for operators who accept the package-manager PATH trust tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: The daemon service PATH history and policy surface is most strongly connected to steipete's repeated work across service-env, install helpers, and gateway doctor docs.
